title: Two application notes of the Erdős #81 series: realizability transfer and exact chordal stability
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the two research notes of the author's Erdős #81 series, in one package. Note I, "From realizability certificates to the Erdős 81 bound": a realizability certificate of Paper V for an auxiliary conflict system whose target is the physical system of copies of K₃ and K₄ in G (conflict when they share an edge, gain C(|K|,2) − 1), with q ≥ 1 classes and budget q·e(G) + cost ≤ q·T + w(X), gives a clique partition of G into pieces of order at most four with at most T pieces (note_I_partition_of_certificate; no chordality); a physical packing with e(G) − g(P) ≤ T does the same (note_I_partition_of_paid_packing); with a certified fractional optimum w, the far branch (e(G) − w < n²/6 − ηn², every η > 0, large n, no chordality) and the near branch (chordal, n ≥ 4·10¹², η = 10⁻¹⁶) give partitions with at most M(n) = ⌊n(n+1)/6⌋ pieces (note_I_far_certificate, note_I_near_certificate); assembled through the transfer, every large chordal graph has such a partition (note_I_erdos81_eventual) and every chordal graph one with at most M(n) + b pieces for an absolute b (note_I_erdos81_all_orders). Note II, "Exact stability for nearly extremal chordal clique partitions": for n large, every chordal graph on n vertices with cp(G) ≤ M(n) and 2000 (M(n) − cp(G)) ≤ n has the root P = {v : n < 2 deg v}, which is a clique, with cp(G) = B(n,|P|) − A − 2m = cp_{≤4}(G), M − cp = (M − B) + A + 2m, edit distance to K_P ∨ I_O equal to A + m and at most M − cp, and (6|P| − 2n − 1)² ≤ 24(M − cp) + 25 (note_II_eventual_root_stability). Seven statements; the thresholds N and the constant b are existential.
